papers.title: Structural Brain Changes Are Linked to Clinical and Cognitive Outcomes in Anti-LGI1 Encephalitis.
papers.reason: The study links widespread structural brain alterations to overall cognition in encephalitis, but it does not isolate executive functions or develop a cognitive process model.

papers.title: Do we measure up? A systematic review of cognitive assessment during a digital era in acquired brain injury.
papers.reason: This review directly evaluates digital, VR, and AR task measures of attention, memory, and executive function in acquired brain injury, including their construct validity.

papers.title: Mechanistic link of obesity to depression and cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.reason: The review concerns molecular pathways underlying general cognitive decline and Alzheimer's pathology rather than executive-function mechanisms or digital assessment.

papers.title: Prevalence and associated factors of cognitive impairment in patients with major depressive disorder: a cross-sectional study in Vietnam.
papers.reason: The study reports executive, fluency, abstraction, and memory impairment in depression, but relies on broad MoCA screening without process-level analysis.

papers.title: Association between caregiving status and cognitive function as well as activities of daily living among community-dwelling older adults with Alzheimer's disease: A cross-sectional study.
papers.reason: The title indicates a general association between caregiving, cognition, and daily functioning in Alzheimer's disease without a specific executive-function or modelling component.

papers.title: Cognitive Well-Being: A Clinical Review of Brain Health, Dementia Risk Reduction, and Emerging Biomarkers for the Osteopathic Family Physician
papers.reason: This is a broad primary-care review of dementia prevention, biomarkers, and treatment with no meaningful focus on executive-function mechanisms or task-based assessment.

papers.title: The dynamic connectome in Alzheimer's disease: From static snapshots to a symphony in time-A hypothesis.
papers.reason: A dynamic-connectome hypothesis may provide general neural context for cognitive decline, but the available information does not establish a specific connection to executive function.

papers.title: A scalable workflow using digital cognitive assessment and pTau217 for MCI detection
papers.reason: The paper combines digital cognitive measurements, machine-learning classification, and a blood biomarker in a scalable workflow for detecting MCI and Alzheimer's pathology.

papers.title: Estimation of Long-Term Care Needs Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults in Indonesia.
papers.reason: The available title concerns estimation of long-term care needs and provides no indication of executive-function modelling, neuroscience, or cognitive biomarker assessment.

papers.title: REmotely monitored, Mobile health-supported Multidomain Rehabilitation with High Intensity Interval Training for COVID-19 (REMM-HIIT-CoV): Trial Design and Rationale.
papers.reason: Cognition is only a secondary MoCA outcome in a remotely monitored physical rehabilitation trial whose primary focus is post-COVID exercise capacity.

papers.title: Bridging data scarcity and explainability in EEG based Alzheimer’s prediction using cGAN augmented GATv2-LSTM networks
papers.reason: This is a close applied match using EEG connectivity and temporal features, synthetic-data augmentation, and explainable deep learning to classify healthy, MCI, Alzheimer's, and FTD groups.

papers.title: Cognitive Impairment Across the Spectrum of Chronic Kidney Disease: Clinical Characteristics and Implications for Practice—Is There a Role for Medical Nutritional Therapy?
papers.reason: The review identifies executive-attentional dysfunction and slowed processing as characteristic of chronic kidney disease and discusses practical executive-function assessment.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Dementia with Lewy Bodies — Current Applications, Diagnostic Challenges, and Future Perspectives
papers.reason: The review covers AI-based integration of cognitive, EEG, imaging, molecular, and digital biomarkers for Lewy body dementia, but offers no new assessment model or empirical validation.

papers.title: Integrative multimodal framework combining undercarboxylated osteocalcin and medial prefrontal cortex morphometry for prediction of cognitive decline in osteoporosis: a machine learning study
papers.reason: The study integrates a circulating biomarker, prefrontal morphometry, and machine learning to predict cognitive decline, although cognition is measured globally rather than through executive tasks.

papers.title: Progress of Digital Technologies in the Perioperative Management of Postoperative Delirium Among Older Adults.
papers.reason: The review discusses machine learning, wearables, and EEG for delirium risk identification, but its focus is perioperative clinical management rather than executive-function assessment.

papers.title: Retinal Optical Coherence Tomography-Angiography and Longitudinal Changes in Cognition and Cerebral Small Vessel Disease
papers.reason: The longitudinal association of retinal vascular measures with MRI markers and MoCA decline supports noninvasive multimodal cognitive monitoring, but it does not specifically assess executive processes.

papers.title: Dataset from Bloom 2.0: task performance, user satisfaction, and open-ended feedback from a web-based assessment platform for executive function and related cognitive processes in higher education
papers.reason: The dataset provides trial-level accuracy, timing, and error measures from six web-based executive-function tasks, enabling secondary work on scalable digital cognitive assessment.

papers.title: The medial prefrontal cortex is required for prospective navigation in spatial sequential memory
papers.reason: The lesion experiment provides causal evidence that medial prefrontal cortex supports prospective trajectory generation by integrating sequential rules with spatial information while sparing retrospective navigation.

papers.title: Factors associated with cognitive impairment among adults with epilepsy: A cross-sectional study of clinical and electroencephalographic findings in Indonesia
papers.reason: The study links abnormal clinical EEG findings to global MoCA-defined cognitive impairment in epilepsy but does not analyze executive domains or relevant EEG mechanisms.

papers.title: Using Cognitive Map Theory to Create a Serious Game Assessment for Cognitive Dysfunction Post-Brain Injury
papers.reason: The paper uses cognitive-map theory to design an ecologically valid serious-game assessment of executive dysfunction after traumatic brain injury.

papers.title: The impact of stress on cognitive functions and quality of life in young and middle-aged
papers.reason: The study finds stress-related impairment on Stroop interference measures despite unchanged global cognition, providing a specific behavioral result about executive control.

papers.title: Leakage-Aware Explainable Alzheimer’s Disease Detection Using Ensemble-Based Tree Models and Shapley Additive Explanations
papers.reason: The paper develops an explainable, leakage-aware dementia classifier combining cognitive scores, demographic variables, and MRI biomarkers, though it is not specific to executive function.

papers.title: Association Between Smartphone-Based IMU Turning Performance and Screening-Defined Mild Cognitive Impairment in Older Adults
papers.reason: The study evaluates smartphone-derived turning time as a digital mobility marker associated with MoCA-defined MCI, but discrimination is modest and executive function is not directly measured.
